description: CCRL-Blitz-anchored opponent pool for absolute Sgurr calibration. Names must match fastchess PGN tags and anchors.txt exactly.
notes: Ratings are single-CPU CCRL Blitz, re-sourced from the live complete list on 2026-08-09. Every engine here is the best-rated version of its family on that list, and each downloaded binary self-reports the exact version the rating belongs to (verified via `id name`).

EXTENDS pool-2026-07-B; it does not replace it. The previous roster is archived verbatim at pool-2026-07-B.json and all nine of its anchors are RETAINED in anchors.txt. Ordo re-solves over ALL accumulated calib-*.pgn, so the historical games against Blunder/Zahak/Weiss/Igel still pin the lower half of the ladder and every older Sgurr version keeps its place on one scale.

Scale consistency was checked before adopting these values rather than assumed: the same live list rates Blunder 8.5.5 at 2663 against pool-B's Blunder-8.0.0 at 2651, i.e. the 2026-08 list sits on the same scale as the 2026-07-15 re-source. No repeat of the pool-A README-sourced inflation (mean ~31 Elo).

WHY THIS POOL EXISTS. v8.2 measured 3058 +/-7 on pool-B but scored 50.8% against Weiss-1.2, its top anchor, and 86-97% against five of the other seven. The pool was saturated: it could not resolve v8.3, and with v8.2 sitting essentially at the ceiling the absolute number was poorly constrained from above. Every engine here is at or above v8.2's measured level (3056 to 3312), so v8.2 is bracketed on both sides for the first time.

SIX NEW FAMILIES, none previously represented. This is the point, not a side effect. The four pool-B anchors disagree by 90 Elo about where v8.2 sits (Igel 3106, Weiss-1.0 3016), and that spread is stable across releases (63/100/90 for v8.0/v8.1/v8.2), so it is systematic rather than sampling. It is what happens when ratings measured under CCRL's conditions are transferred to a different book, time control and machine. Independent implementations carry independent transfer biases, so widening from four families to ten is the only lever that can actually narrow the ~+/-45 systematic uncertainty. Whether it does is the question this run answers.

Opponent strength was capped deliberately. Beyond roughly 250 Elo above v8.2 a game is as uninformative as the 97% walkovers this pool replaces: engines rated 3400+ exist on the same list and were passed over for that reason.

Binaries are the AVX2/BMI2/x86-64-v3 builds throughout, matching the Ryzen 7 7800X3D (Zen 4) the gauntlet runs on and Sgurr's own -march=native build. All six were verified to complete a UCI handshake AND return a legal bestmove under clock-based `go wtime/btime` before being admitted, since a handshake alone does not prove an engine can play and a non-spawning engine forfeits every game while still producing a complete, plausible result.
Pool is append-only: never remove or re-rate an engine within a pool_id -- create a new pool_id instead.
